rationale:
Iteration 7 (mass 0.5 kg) reversed the inertia gain: s-bend finishes fell from 19 to 18, line losses rose from 0.55 to 0.85, and progress fell from 0.996 to 0.965. Iteration 6 (body_length 0.10, mass 0.6, y 0.07, score 657.9) is therefore the best measured geometry. The Builder's proposal restores mass 0.6 and changes only sensor y from 0.07 to 0.075. I accept that geometry. Body length is at its 0.10 m minimum, and the mass floor for this controller is 0.6 kg.

For the controller, I keep the iteration 6 gains exactly: kp 2.8, ki 0.05, kd 0.5, base_speed 1.5, antisymmetric weights [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2] and last_direction line loss. The slalom has sat at its max_error floor (0.063) with 0 finishes through every inertia change, so the look-ahead step is the only variable that can be tested against it. Keeping the controller fixed means any change in the slalom or s-bend can be attributed to y 0.075. The oval has margin (max_error 0.017 against a 0.06 limit), so the extra look-ahead should show up first as higher oval max_error if it adds lag.

Expected, not measured: s-bend holds 19 or more finishes with line losses at or below 0.55; slalom line losses at or below 1.0 with progress above 0.26; oval still 20 of 20. Risk: y 0.075 adds sensing lag, which would show as oval max_error above about 0.025 or s-bend oscillation above 0.35. If either happens, return to y 0.07 for the next iteration.
